package_info.package_name: Azure API Management (APIM) legacy API endpoints
package_info.package_manager: Azure Cloud Platform (not a traditional package manager, but a managed service)
package_info.package_versions: All versions with legacy API endpoints enabled (pre-June 2024 deployments, especially those with legacy ARM API access)
package_info.why_malicious: The legacy API endpoints in Azure API Management allow users with only Reader permissions to escalate privileges and obtain administrative SSO tokens, bypassing intended access controls. This enables attackers to gain full administrative control, access sensitive data, and modify or deploy APIs, representing a critical security risk.

execution_context.file_location: Legacy Azure Resource Manager (ARM) API endpoint (deprecated endpoint, e.g., /providers/Microsoft.ApiManagement/service/{serviceName}/listSecrets)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code issues a GET request to a deprecated ARM API endpoint using only Reader permissions, retrieves an SSO token with full administrative privileges, and enables the attacker to authenticate against the APIM Management API as an admin.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This behavior is suspicious because it allows a low-privilege user (Reader) to obtain an administrative SSO token, which should only be accessible to users with higher privileges.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normally, Reader permissions should not allow access to secrets or administrative tokens. The actual behavior allows privilege escalation and full administrative access.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use would involve an admin retrieving secrets for operational purposes, but never via a Reader role or deprecated endpoint.
key_indicators: Access to listSecrets or SSO token generation with insufficient privileges
API version parameter referencing old versions (e.g., 2016-10-10)

execution_context.trigger: API call (runtime, after obtaining SSO token)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the attacker uses the stolen admin SSO token to authenticate API requests, allowing them to deploy new APIs, modify existing ones, and access all sensitive configuration data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This behavior is suspicious because it leverages a token obtained through privilege escalation to perform high-impact administrative actions.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal API usage requires proper admin authentication. Here, a Reader escalates to admin and performs unauthorized actions.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use would be an actual admin performing these actions, not a Reader.
key_indicators: Use of SSO tokens obtained via deprecated endpoints
Administrative actions performed by accounts with no prior admin privileges

attack_chain.action: Attacker with Reader permissions calls a deprecated ARM API endpoint to retrieve an administrative SSO token.
Attacker uses the admin SSO token to authenticate against the APIM Management API and perform administrative actions (deploy/modify APIs, access secrets, etc.).
attack_chain.leads_to: Full compromise of the APIM service and access to all sensitive data.

behavioral_signatures: API calls to deprecated ARM endpoints (e.g., listSecrets) by users with Reader permissions
Retrieval of SSO tokens or secrets by non-admin accounts
Subsequent administrative API actions from accounts previously limited to Reader role
file_indicators: No direct file indicators (cloud API abuse), but audit logs showing access to /listSecrets or similar endpoints
network_indicators: Unusual API calls to management.azure.com with old API versions (e.g., 2016-10-10)
Burst of administrative API calls from accounts with no prior admin activity
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor Azure audit logs for API calls to deprecated endpoints (such as /listSecrets) by users with Reader permissions. Flag any retrieval of SSO tokens or secrets by non-admin accounts. Correlate subsequent administrative actions (API deployments, modifications, or secret access) performed by accounts that recently escalated privileges via legacy endpoints. Alert on use of old API versions in management API calls.
